item.title: Ask About Our Featured Listings — Wed Sep 30 — LiveMusicAsheville.com
item.description:
Established in February 2019, LiveMusicAsheville.com now reaches thousands of people every week actively searching for live music in the Asheville area. Roughly 60% of our traffic comes from Google Search as we dominate the top of the results for queries such as “Asheville live music” & “live music Asheville”. Meanwhile our direct traffic is experiencing explosive growth, proving more locals are now using us as their go-to music calendar. Our free listings include just the basics of Who’s Playin’ Where & When. Our Featured Listings really stand out among the dozens of events on the calendar every day. While we update every Wednesday for the following Friday thru Thursday, these Featured Listings are published much sooner and include your picture or poster, a description of the event and the venue, website/ticket links and a Google map. We also share these events on our social media stories to help further promote your show.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: COMING OCTOBER 7th | STRFKR w/ Happy Sad Face — Wed Sep 30 — Sierra Nevada Mills River
item.description: Wednesday, October 7 | Amphitheater Stage | 6 PM DOORS | 6:30PM SHOW | From $38.05 Event Details and Tickets Since forming in 2007, STRFKR have been perfecting a style that hides emotional complexities and existential searching in hyper-catchy, melody-forward pop music. The band’s spiritual and philosophical undercurrents never outshine their highly danceable sounds, but both are integral parts of what they do. Over the years and through the course of a discography that includes not just multiple studio albums but a wealth of fan-focused auxiliary releases, STRFKR’s combination of thoughtful lyricism and party starting hooks have made them a consistent success with critical music listeners and show-goers. item.title: Jack’s Old-Time Jam — Wed Sep 30, 5:00 PM — Jack Of The Wood
item.description:
Grab some dinner and a pint while enjoying our long-running Old-Time Jam! Featuring many talented musicians from the local WNC area, our traditional Appalachian mountain music jam runs from 5-9pm every Wednesday night at Jack of the Wood! Jack Of The Wood is still a downtown hot spot for food, brews and drink since 1997 and founders Joan and Joe Eckert who still own it, have maintained the original lively English and Irish vibe. The old-time mountain and Irish music jams continue, including a hot bluegrass jam Thursdays and brunch every Sunday. The venue extends a welcoming feeling to regulars and newcomers to this day. https://jackofthewood.com/
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: The Queen Sessions V5 | Featuring Meschiya Lake — Wed Sep 30, 7:00 PM — Hotel Eve Jazz
item.description: Join us at Hotel Eve for The Queen Sessions, as acclaimed vocalist Meschiya Lake honors one of the greatest inspirations of her nearly two decades of jazz performance: Bessie Smith, “The Empress of the Blues.” Since relocating from her beloved New Orleans to Asheville, Lake has brought with her the music, vitality, and spirit of the birthplace of jazz. A six-time winner of Best Female Vocalist in New Orleans’ premier music awards, including OffBeat and Gambit honors, Lake has earned acclaim both at home and internationally, including the 2019 Danish Music Award for Best Jazz Vocal Album of the Year. For this special Queen Sessions performance, Lake is joined by Asheville jazz ambassadors Andrew Fletcher on piano and Josef Butts on bass for an intimate evening celebrating the music and legacy of Bessie Smith. item.title: Choosing Peace After Loss: Israel/Palestine, Civil Discourse, and the Courage to Listen — Sun Oct 4, 2:00 PM
item.description:
The UNC Asheville Center for Jewish Studies presents Aziz Abu Sarah, co-author of “The Future Is Peace: A Shared Journey Across the Holy Land.” Drawing from his experiences and work in peacebuilding, Abu Sarah will explore nonviolence, dialogue, shared humanity, and the possibility of choosing peace after profound loss. The presentation will be followed by a book signing. This event is free and open to the public and will take place in the Blue Ridge Room of Highsmith Student Union. Click here to register for this event.
Accessibility UNC Asheville is committed to providing universal access to all of our events. If you have any questions about access or would like to request reasonable accommodations that will facilitate your full participation in the film screenings, please contact Stephanie Bullick, Director of Accessibility, at accessibility@unca.edu.
Source: UNC Asheville
